A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PerturbODE work. All 28 pages of v3 and 39 pages of v4, including appendices, figures, tables, equations, and v4's checklist, support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original SERGIO simulation experiments, TF Atlas network inference and intervention predictions, and appendix ablations and resampling analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds BoolODE experiments, ChIP-Atlas validation, and additional baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same neural ODE, module factorization, intervention mechanisms, Wasserstein training objective, sparsity penalty, and optional diffusion regularization. The expanded evaluations do not establish a change to PerturbODE.

E1.justification: v4 adds a 10-gene cyclic BoolODE benchmark with activating and repressing interactions. It also evaluates TF Atlas predictions against a 223-gene ChIP-Atlas reference containing positive and negative edges, extending v3's acyclic simulations and positive-edge human references.

E2.justification: GENIE3 joins the retained SERGIO and TF Atlas network comparisons. The held-out intervention experiment expands from NO-TEARS and NO-TEARS-LR to include GEARS, scGPT, and the Ahlmann-Eltze linear baseline. These methods have reported results, rather than merely new citations.

E3.justification: v4 replaces Pearson correlation with cell-type distance and introduces BoolODE simulation and unsigned-edge evaluation protocols. PerturbODE threshold multipliers increase tenfold: yeast 0.1 to 1, and random-DAG/TF Atlas 0.01 to 0.1. Reported TF Atlas dimensionality changes from 817 to 812; the appendix's highly variable gene count changes from 817 to 500, already stated in v3's main text. These revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds a false-discovery analysis across three sparsity/threshold settings using ChIP-Atlas (Table 1) and revises prediction visualizations. Existing module-count, perturbation-count, sparsity-penalty, enrichment, bootstrap, and split-stability analyses largely carry over, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: v4 explicitly reports five runs for the yeast and BoolODE benchmarks and labels held-out prediction summaries as median plus standard deviation. This does not establish an increase in runs for retained experiments. Existing mean/standard-deviation tables, random-graph significance testing, 105 bootstraps, and 133 train-validation splits remain.

E6.justification: v4 adds BoolODE, ChIP-Atlas, comparator, and cell-type results while removing Pearson results. Table 2a reports GEARS W2 of 65 versus PerturbODE's 84. Retained tables also change: yeast predicted edges fall from 43,655.0 to 1,205.8 under revised thresholds, and Table 5 replaces v3's duplicated yeast values with different random-DAG entries. These are added or revised reports, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.16 newly defines cell-type distance through nearest-neighbor classification probabilities and their L1 distance; A.13 adds the BoolODE stochastic equations. The existing PerturbODE mathematics, SERGIO derivation, stability reasoning, and identifiability discussion remain, with no new proof.

C1.justification: The central claims remain scalable, interpretable GRN discovery and trajectory prediction using neural ODEs, including cycles and unseen interventions. v4 makes unseen-intervention simulation explicit in the abstract, but v3 already claims it in the introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: v4 acknowledges large prediction errors when PerturbODE fails, discusses GEARS's lower Wasserstein error and use of GO priors, and interprets the new low-dimensional and false-discovery comparisons. Appendix A.1 adds a wet-lab validation requirement before downstream decisions. Existing identifiability and stability qualifications remain.

D1.justification: v4 supplies implementation references and hyperparameters for GENIE3, GEARS, and scGPT, BoolODE generation settings, and GPU/CPU memory and runtime limits in A.17. The checklist states that reproduction code will be released. These extend documentation; the existing PerturbODE solver and training specifications remain essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for the linear prediction baseline, GEARS, scGPT, and ChIP-Atlas, while removing the PIDC and GRNBoost2 references. Its broader positioning relative to causal graph discovery and neural ODE research remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 applies targeted copyediting and results rewrites, promotes held-out prediction to Section 4.3, consolidates module interpretation and enrichment in Appendix A.11, and regroups threshold details. It also updates author information and adds a checklist. Most method and discussion prose is retained.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive figure and table rearrangement. Figure 1 is redrawn, new benchmark displays appear, comparator plots and legends expand, prediction summaries become paired subtables, and enrichment and training visualizations move to the appendix. These changes substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens evaluation of the paper's central promises. Compared with v3's acyclic simulations, positive-only human references, and two linear prediction comparators, it tests cyclic networks, false discoveries, and competitiveness against stronger prediction methods, exposing limitations as well as strengths. Additional implementation and resource disclosures help reproducibility. Numerical inconsistencies remain—for example, NO-TEARS has W2 396 in Table 2a but a median of 164.75 from Table 2b—yet the broader, more informative validation provides a substantial overall gain.
